newsitem.title: UK: Dana Petroleum to buy Seafield.
newsitem.headline: Dana Petroleum to buy Seafield.

text.p: Dana Petroleum Plc has made a recommended takeover offer for Seafield Resources Plc, valuing the group at 54.5 million stg.

The offer is on the basis of 10 new Dana shares for every three Seafield shares, valuing them at 78.3 pence per share based on Dana's closing share price of 23.5 pence last night. A full cash alternative offer of 72 pence per Seafield share is also available.
Dana has received undertakings to accept the offer in respect of 34,903,186 Seafield shares, representing 50 percent of the share capital. This includes the shares of Seafield directors.

Seafield said in a statement "There is a good fit between the two companies in terms of production and earnings profiles. The enlarged group will have an improved asset balance in terms of exploration versus production, oil versus gas and geographical location, thereby providing a solid foundation for future growth."
Charles Smith, Dana chairman, said "This deal represents a decisive step in line with Dana's strategy to expand into carefully selected international areas..."
John Raitt, Seafield chairman, added that he was confident the two could work well together.
